about: Server-only, saved (models game.crowds.v0/v1 16 bytes, v2 12 bytes align 4; no member names known). Lives on crowd character triggers (esv::CrowdCharacterTrigger), up to 212 holders, from level load on. Driven by esv::crowds::SpawnSystem::ProcessTriggers / SpawnCharacters (EoCServer.dll, CrowdCharacterSpawnSystem.cpp): a spawn timer per trigger, the number of characters it has spawned, and a flag that blocks spawning while players are near.

evidence.says: EoCServer.dll+0xD73760 ProcessTriggers: while the float at state+4 is less than the float at state+0 the trigger keeps waiting, otherwise it spawns; i.e. +0 is the time to wait before the next spawn (re-rolled with ls::Random). macOS Save copies 8 bytes (+0..+8) to the v2 model. Live floats 0 .. 24.6
ProcessTriggers: adds the frame's delta time to the float at state+4 when no blocking query matches; compared with +0. Live floats 0 .. 2910

SpawnCharacters EoCServer.dll+0xD74A30: checks that the unsigned 16-bit count at state+8 plus the new count stays at or below the trigger max (CrowdCharacterTrigger +0x7C scaled by crowd quality); ProcessTriggers compares the trigger's max with the unsigned 16-bit value at state+8. macOS Save copies a 2-byte value from +8. Live 0

ProcessTriggers: stores in the bool at state+10 the result of a distance-to-players test (one computed float compared as less than another) and spawning is skipped while it is set; written from EoCServer.dll+0xD72950 (called with the players and the transform). macOS Save copies one byte from +0xA. Live 0

open_questions: exact meaning of the bool at +0xA (players near / in view)
whether +0 is an interval or a target time; units seconds
